subsystems.name: Compute die
subsystems.role: the chip itself: thousands of small cores that run the same instruction across many data points at once.

subsystems.name: Memory subsystem
subsystems.role: feeds the cores fast enough that they are not starved of data.

subsystems.name: Board and interface
subsystems.role: carries power and data between the GPU, the motherboard and the display.
parts: display outputs such as DisplayPort and HDMI

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: converts the 12 V (or higher) input into the sub-1 V the die needs at hundreds of amps.

subsystems.name: Thermal solution
subsystems.role: removes hundreds of watts of heat from a small piece of silicon.

subsystems.name: Firmware and driver stack
subsystems.role: turns silicon into a usable device for games, video and AI workloads.

buildSteps.title: Design the chip
buildSteps.detail: Engineers describe the logic in a hardware description language, verify it in simulation for months, then place and route billions of transistors into a physical layout.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the wafers
buildSteps.detail: A foundry prints each layer of the circuit onto silicon wafers using deep-ultraviolet and extreme-ultraviolet lithography, in a process that takes weeks per wafer.

buildSteps.title: Test and dice
buildSteps.detail: Each die is probed on the wafer; faulty ones are marked and good ones are cut apart.

buildSteps.title: Package the die
buildSteps.detail: The GPU die and its memory are flip-chip bonded onto a substrate — often several dies and HBM stacks on a silicon interposer — then sealed under a lid.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the board
buildSteps.detail: Surface-mount machines place the packaged module, memory, regulators and connectors on the PCB, which then passes through a reflow oven.

buildSteps.title: Fit the cooler
buildSteps.detail: Thermal paste or pad, heatsink or vapour chamber, fans and shroud are attached, and the shroud is tested for noise and airflow.

buildSteps.title: Qualify and bin
buildSteps.detail: Every card is run under load; those that pass at higher clocks or are fully functional are sold as premium models, others are downrated.

buildSteps.title: Ship software
buildSteps.detail: Drivers and firmware are written, validated against thousands of games and applications, and released alongside the hardware.

prerequisites.tech: Leading-edge logic fabrication (7 nm class and below)
prerequisites.why: only a handful of foundries can pattern features this small at volume.
needed to print the finest layers without excessive multi-patterning.
stacked memory on an interposer gives the bandwidth that wide AI and graphics workloads need.
lets multiple dies and memory stacks sit in one package when a single die has hit its size limit.

prerequisites.tech: Mature EDA tools and IP libraries
prerequisites.why: no team can verify or lay out a modern GPU by hand.

pathway.milestone: chiplet-based flagships with HBM and dedicated matrix-maths units
pathway.unlocks: training and running large AI models on a single accelerator.

pathway.milestone: 3D stacking of logic and cache dies
pathway.unlocks: less energy spent moving data on and off the package.

pathway.milestone: co-packaged optics connecting accelerators across racks
pathway.unlocks: clusters of tens of thousands of GPUs working as one machine without copper bottlenecks.
higher efficiency for specialised workloads, with the GPU as the flexible fallback.
